subject: Secure multitenant sidecar communication – architectural clarifications
messages:
From: Paul Ramirez <paul.ramirez@acme-corp.com>

Cc: security@acme-corp.com

Subject: Clarification on sidecar comms and tenant isolation for RFI

Diego,

Thanks for the RFI package — the diagrams were helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our architecture/security team about your proposed sidecar model:

1) How do you terminate TLS between host and model sidecar? Do you use a shared CA, per-tenant mTLS certs, or workload identity (e.g., SPIFFE)?
2) If the sidecar proxies outbound requests (egress to external services and to other tenants), how are tenant-boundaries enforced at the network and proxy layers?
3) What does KV cache sharing look like? We want to ensure no cross-tenant leakage when caching prefixes or shard keys.

Can you send a short architecture note (or updated diagram) that explains the cert lifecycle, SNI handling, and any ACLs enforced at the envoy/sidecar layer? We have a 20-person security review next Wednesday and would like to include your answers.

Appreciate it —
Paul

Paul —

Thanks for the precise questions, and great to hear you found the RFI useful. High-level answers below; attaching a clarified diagram (sidecar-comm-diagram-v2.png) that calls out cert flows and data-plane ACLs. Monica and Markus are looped in for deeper tech details.

1) TLS termination and identity
- We use mutual TLS between runtime host and the model-serving sidecar. Certificates are short-lived (default 24 hours) issued by the Redwood CA issued by our control plane.
- For private deployments (VPC/on-prem), we support customer-managed PKI and can integrate with SPIFFE/SVID for workload identity instead of Redwood CA.
- Each sidecar instance gets a tenant-scoped SAN (subjectAltName) and an explicit tenant ID in the cert; the control plane revokes/rotates certs automatically.

2) Tenant boundary enforcement (data plane)
- Sidecars run in the same pod/VM as model workers but enforce tenant isolation at three levels:
  a) mTLS + tenant SAN: remote peers validate SAN and tenant claim before accepting requests.
  b) Envoy-based ACLs: per-tenant routing table that restricts upstream clusters to allowed endpoints and enforces SNI-based virtual hosts.
  c) Kernel-level namespace and iptables rules for egress segmentation when running on customer hosts.

3) KV cache and prefix isolation
- Cache keys are namespaced by tenant ID and model version. The cache layer prefixes keys with a tenant-specific namespace token which is cryptographically derived from the tenant identity to prevent accidental collisions.
- We do not expose any cross-tenant cache invalidation APIs; cache telemetry and evictions are global but keys remain namespaced.

We've attached the updated architecture diagram explaining cert lifecycle, SNI flows, and the envoy filter chain. If desirable, Markus can provide a short threat-model appendix describing detection/mitigation of sidecar impersonation and cache poisoning.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Paul — quick follow-up with implementation specifics you can drop into your review doc. Quoted below are the items Diego summarized with concrete config points and mitigations.

> 1) TLS termination and identity
> - mutual TLS between runtime host and model-serving sidecar. Certificates are short-lived (default 24 hours) issued by the Redwood CA...

Implementation details:
- Cert issuance: control-plane issues a CSR signed by Redwood CA. CSR includes tenant-id and instance-instance-id. Default TTL 24h; configurable down to 1h for high-security customers.
- Rotation: rolling rotation agent runs in the sidecar; failures cause the sidecar to block new incoming sessions and return 5xx until rotated successfully.
- SPIFFE/Customer PKI: for Private installs we integrate with customer SPIRE server or an on-prem CA via ACME/PKCS#11.

> 2) Tenant boundary enforcement (data plane)

Implementation details:
- Envoy filters: we deploy a custom authn filter that enforces tenant SAN and a tenant claim header (x-tenant-id). The filter rejects any request where SAN != x-tenant-id.
- SNI handling: SNI is mapped to tenant-scoped virtual hosts; SNI spoofing is mitigated because mTLS validation requires cert SAN match and the envoy RBAC rejects mismatch.
- Egress policies: per-tenant egress policy bundles are pushed from the control plane; each bundle contains allowed CIDRs and service FQDNs. Unlisted destinations are denied by default.

Risk mitigations (threat model highlights):
- Sidecar impersonation: detection via certificate transparency-like audit logs at the control plane and short cert TTLs reduce window of misuse.
- Cache poisoning: keys cryptographically namespaced + HMAC guard on external cache keys; cache telemetry emits anomalies when collision rates spike.

If you want, we can produce a one-page threat model appendix with attack trees and mitigations. Markus volunteered to take that item.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
